Subject: Short-term QoS lane + provisional credit for launch

Hi Hannah —

We're ramping up for a targeted product launch next week and expect a sharp 48-72 hour spike in inference traffic (estimated 2.1B tokens over baseline). Our engineering team is worried about hitting our current quota and being throttled mid-launch.

Two asks:
- Can Redwood provision a short-term QoS lane (temporary quota top-up) starting Monday 10/12 through 10/15?
- Given this is an onboarding/launch event, are you able to offer a provisional credit or rebate on overrun charges if usage is within the forecasted window? We can share traffic patterns and a mutual action plan.

We're on a committed monthly tier today but this is a one-off scaling event. Time is tight — procurement will need wording for PO/signature if terms include credits.

Appreciate quick guidance.

—Alex
VP Product, Gridly

Alex —

Thanks for the heads up and for the traffic summary attachment. Short answer: yes, we can provision a temporary QoS/top-up lane. We generally handle these with a short-term uplift + one-time overrun true-up and, for launch-critical customers, a provisional credit tied to a PO and a brief post-launch reconciliation.

Proposed path:
- Temporary QoS lane: +3x quota for 72 hours (10/12 00:00 UTC → 10/15 00:00 UTC).
- Pricing: usage during that window billed at existing committed rate; any measured overrun beyond the uplift is normally invoiced on next cycle.
- Provisional credit: Redwood can earmark a one-time credit up to 25% of the estimated overrun charge, subject to an after-action reconciliation (we'll compare forecast vs actual and adjust). Credit issued only after PO references the amendment and acceptance of the reconciliation terms.

If that sounds acceptable, I'll loop in our billing lead (Ben) and partner success (Jonas) to finalize wording and produce a short amendment document you can attach to the PO.

Quick Qs for your team: can you confirm expected peak QPS and affinity to a single region (us-west vs us-east)? That helps kernel selection and capacity routing.

Best,
Hannah
Head of GTM, Redwood Inference
